_comment: Single source of truth for what Collaborate needs in Entra. Edit ONLY here: Deploy-Collaborate.ps1 and Update-Collaborate.ps1 both reconcile against this file and grant whatever is missing (idempotent). 'appRoles' and 'directoryRoles' are granted to the Function App's MANAGED IDENTITY and cover administration. 'delegatedScopes' are granted to the PORTAL APP REGISTRATION and are only ever used on behalf of a signed-in user, so Graph enforces that user's own rights. Granting still needs the operator to be Global Administrator or Privileged Role Administrator.

appRoles.reason: create B2B invitations on behalf of employees who cannot invite themselves
read guests, write the expiry date to the extension attribute, block sign-in, set the sponsor
delete a guest once the grace period lapses, and restore one that is renewed in time
resolve the inviter group, verified domains, guest search and the owner people picker
signInActivity for inactive-guest cleanup, and invite events when adopting guests that predate the tool

read the tenant's external sharing capability and allowed/blocked domain lists, so a share that cannot possibly work is refused before a guest account is created. Read-only, and tenant-level only: SharePoint does not expose the per-site setting through Graph

directoryRoles.reason: invitations keep working when the tenant restricts guest invitations to admin roles, which is exactly the tenant this tool is built for

delegatedScopes.reason: identify the signed-in user on the delegated path
find the SharePoint sites the user can already see, for the picker
browse the user's own files and grant a guest access to one of them, as that user
add a guest to a Team the user owns, as that user
the group membership behind a Team add, as that user
read a Team's web address so the guest gets a link straight into it rather than the generic Teams page; the tool works without this and falls back

read a site's own settings (external sharing, lock state) as the signed-in user. Graph does not expose them, and the tenant admin API needs SharePoint administrator rights an employee does not have. Read-only

send an invitation from the inviter's own mailbox, when the tenant has chosen that. Requested by the PORTAL in the browser, never by the Function App: a delegated Mail.Send used server-side would appear to Conditional Access as a sign-in from a datacentre, and an application Mail.Send on the managed identity would let this tool send as anybody
